name: Campfire Crunchwraps
desc: Crunchwraps prepped at home and folded at camp, crisped seam side down in a skillet over the fire or a camp stove.

source.title: Campfire Crunchwraps
source.evidence: Saved Instagram reel; caption and on-screen text captured in the owner's saved-recipes export

ingredients.raw: 6 more large flour tortillas, trimmed into 6-inch rounds
1 tbsp neutral oil, for the skillet

steps: At home: heat the oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat and cook the onion until translucent, about 4 minutes. Add the beef and cook, breaking it up, until no pink remains (160°F).
Stir in the taco seasoning and water and simmer on low 7-8 minutes, until the sauce coats the meat. Cool, then pack in a sealed container.
Pack the tomatoes, lettuce, cheese, cheese sauce and sour cream in separate containers. Keep everything in a cooler at 40°F or below.
Using a small plate as a template, trim 6 tortillas into 6-inch rounds (the small rounds). Bag them with the large tortillas and tostadas.
At camp: lay a large tortilla flat. Add a scant 1/2 cup of beef, a spoonful of cheese sauce, a tostada, a little sour cream, lettuce, tomato and shredded cheese.
Set a small tortilla round on top and fold the edges of the large tortilla toward the center in a circle, pleating as you go, so the round holds the folds closed.

Heat a lightly oiled cast iron skillet over a medium-low camp stove flame or on a grate over coals. Cook seam side down 2-3 minutes, until golden, then flip and cook 2-3 minutes more, until crisp and the beef is hot through.
tips: The small tortilla round is the key step: it gives the fold enough tortilla to stay closed on the grill.
Go light on filling for a tight fold; overfilled wraps split.
She also makes Dutch oven nachos with the pot lined in parchment for cleanup.
